questions.why: Fringe shift = (mu-1)t/lambda. Given shift equals one full fringe width, mu = 1 + lambda/t = 1 + 589.3/1100 = 1.54.

questions.question: Brilliant colours observed on thin films of oily surface and soapy water arise due to the optical phenomenon of ______.
questions.why: Thin-film colours are caused by interference between light reflected from the top and bottom surfaces of the thin film.

questions.question: In a toy factory, machines A, B and C manufacture 30%, 40%, 30% of the output respectively. 2%, 3%, 1% of their respective outputs are defective. A toy is found defective. The probability that it was taken from machine B is:
questions.why: Bayes theorem: P(def)=0.3x0.02+0.4x0.03+0.3x0.01=0.021. P(B|def)=0.012/0.021=4/7. Verified computationally.

questions.question: In a triangle ABC, if AB=5, BC=3 and CA=4, then the value of sin(A/2)+tan(A/2) is:
questions.why: 3-4-5 right triangle, right angle at C. cosA=4/5, sinA=3/5 from the right-triangle ratios. Half-angle formulas give sin(A/2)=1/sqrt(10), tan(A/2)=1/3. Sum = (3+sqrt10)/(3sqrt10). Verified exactly by hand and symbolically.

questions.question: Sunlight filtering through the space between the leaves of a tree often makes circular patches on the ground due to ______.
options: the phenomenon of refraction of light
the phenomenon of diffraction of light
the space between the leaves through which sunlight penetrates
the phenomenon of scattering of light
questions.why: Official key says diffraction. WORTH FLAGGING: many physics sources instead attribute this to the pinhole-camera effect (rectilinear propagation forming a small image of the sun through a small gap), not diffraction -- a genuinely disputed attribution in Indian exam circles. Know the key's answer but treat the physics as debated.

questions.question: The longest wavelength of the ultrasonic waves in air at room temperature is nearly:
questions.why: Ultrasonic range starts at 20kHz (upper limit of human hearing). Longest wavelength = lowest frequency in range: lambda=v/f=343/20000 approx 17mm.

questions.question: If two dice are thrown, then the probability that at least one of the dice shows a number less than 5 is:
Which one of the following particles in motion, having same velocity, has the longest wavelength?
questions.why: de Broglie wavelength lambda=h/(mv). For fixed v, lambda is inversely proportional to mass, so the lightest particle (electron) has the longest wavelength.

questions.question: A fast moving electron can have the speed ______.
options: slightly less than the speed of light in vacuum
equal to the speed of sound in air
equal to the speed of light in vacuum
slightly more than the speed of light in vacuum
questions.why: Special relativity forbids any massive particle from reaching or exceeding c; an electron can only approach it asymptotically.

questions.question: If lim(x to infinity)[ax+(7-sqrt3*x^2)/(3-x)]=b, a finite number, then the values of a and b are:
questions.why: Only a=-sqrt3 cancels the x^2 divergence, giving a finite limit of exactly 3*sqrt3. Verified symbolically (sympy): other candidate a values diverge to +/- infinity.

questions.question: ______ manages issues broadly related to recruiting, hiring, training, evaluating and rewarding employees.
questions.why: This is the textbook definition of the Human Resource function.

questions.question: The greatest value of 5sin^2(x)+7cos^2(x)-4sinx*cosx will be:
questions.why: Simplifies to 6+cos(2x)-2sin(2x). Max of A+Bcos(theta)+Csin(theta) form is A+sqrt(B^2+C^2)=6+sqrt(1+4)=6+sqrt5. Verified numerically.

questions.question: Which one of the following optical phenomena gives evidence that light waves are transverse?
questions.why: Only transverse waves can be polarized (having an oscillation direction perpendicular to propagation that can be selectively filtered). Longitudinal waves cannot be polarized.

questions.question: Laser beam is highly intense, monochromatic and coherent, and can be used in monochromatic light experiments for the phenomenon of ______.
questions.why: Interference experiments specifically require monochromatic, coherent sources -- exactly what a laser provides, making it ideal for this over the other listed phenomena.

questions.question: In a piezoelectric generator, the quartz crystal oscillates at its natural LC tank frequency to produce ultrasonic waves of 1MHz, with a capacitance of 25nF in the tank circuit. The inductance of the coil is nearly:
questions.why: f=1/(2*pi*sqrt(LC)) rearranges to L=1/((2*pi*f)^2*C). Computed: L approx 1.013 uH, rounds to 1uH. Verified computationally.

questions.question: Heisenberg's uncertainty principle holds true for all canonically conjugate physical quantities. For which pair does the uncertainty relation CANNOT hold true?
questions.why: Position-momentum, angular-momentum-angle, and energy-time are genuine canonically conjugate pairs. Angle is conjugate to ANGULAR momentum, not linear momentum, so that pairing fails.

questions.question: For two events A and B, which of the following relations is true?
questions.why: De Morgan: A'UB'=(A intersect B)'. So P(A'UB')=1-P(A intersect B)=1-P(A)P(B/A) by the definition of conditional probability.

questions.question: All of the following are key features of management, EXCEPT:
questions.why: Management is a CONTINUOUS process, not a one-time event -- that is the false statement among genuine features of management.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements regarding magnetic materials is NOT correct?
options: Diamagnetic susceptibility is independent of temperature
Ferromagnetic susceptibility is dependent on temperature
Paramagnetic susceptibility is independent of temperature
Paramagnetic susceptibility is dependent on temperature
questions.why: Paramagnetic susceptibility follows Curie's law, chi=C/T -- it IS temperature-dependent, making 'independent of temperature' the false statement (the one the question asks for).

questions.question: The state of population inversion, necessary for laser action with stimulated emission, used in solid state lasers is achieved by ______.
questions.why: Solid-state lasers (e.g. ruby) achieve population inversion via optical pumping; gas lasers typically use electrical discharge instead.

questions.question: The speed of a fast moving electron with energy 3 MeV, in terms of speed of light in vacuum c, is:
questions.why: Total energy E=rest energy(0.511MeV)+KE(3MeV)=3.511MeV. gamma=E/E0=6.87. v/c=sqrt(1-1/gamma^2)=0.989, closest to 0.985c. Verified computationally.

questions.question: Total energy of a moving particle is twice its rest mass energy. The ratio of its relativistic speed to the speed of light in vacuum will be:
questions.why: Total energy = 2x rest energy means gamma=2. v/c=sqrt(1-1/gamma^2)=sqrt(1-1/4)=sqrt(3)/2, i.e. sqrt3:2. Verified exactly.

questions.question: Solution of differential equation e^(x+y)dx + e^(y-2x)dy=0 will be ______, where c is an arbitrary constant.
questions.why: Separating variables and integrating gives y=C1-e^(3x)/3, i.e. 3y+e^(3x)=c after clearing the fraction. Verified symbolically.

questions.question: If the lines x+2y+1=0, 8x+12y+k=0, 3x-2y+5=0 are concurrent, then the value of k is:
questions.why: Find the intersection of the first and third lines: (-3/2, 1/4). Substituting into the second line's equation solves to k=9. Verified computationally.

questions.question: If the ratio of surface area to volume of a cuboid is sqrt3, then the sum of reciprocals of the three sides (length, breadth, height) will be:
questions.why: SA/V=2(1/l+1/b+1/h) always, for any cuboid. Given SA/V=sqrt3, sum of reciprocals=sqrt3/2=sin(pi/3) -- an elegant identity dressed up as a geometry question.

questions.question: Which among the following functions generates revenues for an organisation by selling products and encouraging or stimulating purchases?
questions.why: Marketing is the function directly responsible for demand generation and sales, distinct from operations/finance/HR.

questions.question: The linear equation in two variables x and y, 6x+22y=14 will have:
questions.why: Simplifies to 3x+11y=7. gcd(3,11)=1 divides 7, so this Diophantine equation has integer solutions. A single 2-variable linear equation always has infinitely many real solutions, but the question specifically asks about integer-valued ones.

questions.question: Which among the following is the first task of Strategic Planning?
options: Developing a strategic vision and a business mission
Crafting a strategy to achieve the objectives
Identifying and setting priorities for the execution of strategies
questions.why: Standard strategic-management sequence: vision/mission comes BEFORE objectives, which come before strategy crafting, which comes before execution.

questions.question: For what value of alpha+beta will the three points (alpha,beta), (5,0), (0,5) be collinear?
questions.why: Line through (5,0) and (0,5) is x+y=5. For (alpha,beta) to lie on it, alpha+beta=5 directly.

questions.question: Personnel Management consists of all of the following, EXCEPT:
questions.why: Training, recruitment, and manpower planning are core personnel-management functions; 'administration of earning' falls outside its standard scope.

questions.question: The area enclosed by a complete hysteresis loop on the B-H curve of a ferromagnetic material denotes ______.
options: the energy dissipated in taking the specimen through each complete cycle of magnetisation
questions.why: Standard result: hysteresis loop area = energy lost as heat per magnetization cycle, not any single point-value like coercivity or retentivity.

questions.question: All of the following are methods of grapevine communication, EXCEPT:
questions.why: Cluster, star, and single chain are all informal grapevine communication patterns. Policy circulars are FORMAL communication, the odd one out.

questions.question: The coefficient of x^12 in the expansion of (3x^2+1/x)^30 is:
questions.why: General term T(r+1)=C(30,r)*3^(30-r)*x^(60-3r). Setting 60-3r=12 gives r=16, so coefficient=C(30,16)*3^14. Verified by direct computation.

questions.question: The phenomenon of polarization CANNOT occur in ______.
questions.why: Polarization is only possible for transverse waves. Radio waves, x-rays, and visible light are all transverse EM waves; acoustic (sound) waves are longitudinal and cannot be polarized.

questions.question: The value of 2*tan^-1(2/3) + cos^-1(12/13) is:
questions.why: Numerically verified to equal exactly pi/2 -- a classic inverse-trig identity question.

questions.question: A ______ may be defined as an occupation that requires specialised knowledge and intensive academic preparation, and to which entry is regulated by a representative body.
questions.why: This is the standard definition of 'profession' as distinct from a hobby, passion, or goal.

questions.question: If 37 and 43 are the means of two samples of size 13 and 17 respectively, then the mean of their combined sample will be:
questions.why: Weighted average: (13x37+17x43)/(13+17)=(481+731)/30=1212/30=40.4. Verified exactly.

questions.question: A proton and an alpha particle are accelerated through the same potential difference. The ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths is:
questions.why: lambda=h/sqrt(2mqV). Ratio lambda_proton:lambda_alpha = sqrt(m_alpha*q_alpha/(m_proton*q_proton)) = sqrt(4x2)=2sqrt2:1. Verified.

questions.question: In a Young's double slit set-up with sodium light, if the entire set-up is displaced from air into clear water, the fringe pattern will likely ______.
questions.why: Fringe width is proportional to wavelength, and wavelength shrinks in a denser medium (lambda_water=lambda_air/n). Fringes shrink considerably.

questions.question: Which level of management devotes more time to planning and coordinating functions?
questions.why: Top management is primarily concerned with strategic planning and coordination; lower/entry levels focus more on operational execution.

questions.question: The value of k, for which the system x+2y-3z=0, 2x+y+z=0, x-y+kz=0 has a non-trivial solution, will be:
questions.why: A homogeneous system has non-trivial solutions only when its coefficient determinant is zero. Determinant = 12-3k = 0 gives k=4. Verified computationally.

questions.question: The working of a Nicol prism is based on the optical phenomenon of ______.
questions.why: A Nicol prism uses calcite's double refraction (birefringence) combined with total internal reflection to isolate a single plane-polarized ray.

questions.question: If one root of the quadratic equation x^2-8tx-25=0 is 3+4t, then the other root must be:
questions.why: Sum of roots = -b/a = 8t. Other root = 8t - (3+4t) = -3+4t.

questions.question: The sum of the series 1+2(a^2+1)+3(a^2+1)^2+4(a^2+1)^3 will be:
questions.why: Official key answer is 1/a^4. FLAGGED: could not independently re-derive this closed form from the literal series as transcribed from the scan -- tested the literal 4-term finite sum and it does NOT equal 1/a^4 in general (matched only by coincidence at one specific a value). Likely an infinite series or a sign/exponent detail was lost in transcription. Re-verify against a clean source before trusting fully.

questions.question: What is the term used for the process of passing information, experience, opinion, etc. from one person to another, which is also a bridge of understanding?
questions.why: This is the standard definition of communication as an organisational function.

questions.question: The distance of the highest point on the graph of the function y=12cosx-5sinx from the x-axis is:
questions.why: For y=Acosx+Bsinx, the amplitude (max distance from axis) = sqrt(A^2+B^2) = sqrt(144+25) = sqrt(169) = 13.

questions.question: What is the full form of MIS?
questions.why: MIS = Management Information System, a core business-management acronym.

questions.question: Let f(x,y)=0 represent a circle. If f(0,a) has roots a=2,3 and f(a,0) has roots a=12,1/2, then the centre of the circle is:
questions.why: On the y-axis, sum of roots 2+3=5=-2f gives f=-5/2; product 6=c. On the x-axis, sum of roots 12+0.5=12.5=-2g gives g=-25/4; product 6=c (consistent). Centre=(-g,-f)=(25/4,5/2). Verified computationally.

questions.question: In a dielectric medium, the dielectric polarization P, electric displacement D and electric field E are related as:
questions.why: D = epsilon0*E + P is the defining relation of electric displacement field in a dielectric.

questions.question: The characteristic impedance, as the ratio of amplitudes of E- and H-vectors, of a plane electromagnetic wave in free space is nearly:
questions.why: Z0=sqrt(mu0/epsilon0) is a fundamental physical constant, approximately 376.7 ohm.

questions.question: In order to study the internal atomic structure of crystals, we make use of electromagnetic radiations as ______.
questions.why: X-ray wavelengths match interatomic spacing, enabling diffraction-based crystallography (Bragg's law), unlike visible or UV light.

questions.question: ______ is any plan of action intended to achieve a major or overall aim and also to beat the competition.
questions.why: This is the standard definition of strategy in business management.

questions.question: Which is the apex banking institution for providing finance for agriculture and rural development in India?
questions.why: NABARD = National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development. RBI is the central/monetary authority, SEBI regulates securities markets, IBRD is the World Bank's lending arm — none of them do agri/rural refinancing.

questions.question: As per the 2011 Census, ______ has the highest percentage of households having electricity as a source of lighting and power.
questions.why: Small UTs with near-total household coverage often beat large states on percentage-based census metrics — don't default to the biggest/richest-sounding state.
questions.status: stale: check 2011 census figure currency before reusing

questions.question: Which of the following ancient poet wrote Abhijnanashakuntalam?
questions.why: Kalidasa's best-known Sanskrit play. Aryabhat is a mathematician/astronomer (Aryabhatiya), a common wrong-pick when options mix poets and scientists.

questions.question: What was Tauhid-i-Ilahi?
options: A new religion set up by emperor Akbar
A religious tax imposed by Aurangazeb
questions.why: Akbar's syncretic faith blending elements of Islam, Hinduism, Zoroastrianism, and Christianity — not a tax (that's Jizya, reimposed by Aurangzeb) and not a book.

questions.question: Which statement about the President of India is not correct?
options: The President is the head of the government.
The President is the highest executive authority in the country.
The President appoints the Prime Minister.
The President of India enjoys only nominal powers.
questions.why: Trap pair — President is head of STATE, the Prime Minister is head of GOVERNMENT. Mixing these two up is the single most common civics confusion in Indian polity MCQs.
questions.attempted: wrong (chose 3) (29 Aug 2026) — cleared after re-explain, follow-up check correct

questions.question: India has a ______ system.
questions.why: India has many recognized national and state parties contesting simultaneously — not a US-style two-party system.

questions.question: Which type of house is not correctly paired with the region where it is built?
questions.why: Houseboats are traditionally associated with Kashmir and South-East Asia (e.g. Kerala backwaters), not Sub-Saharan Africa — a plausible-sounding but wrong region pairing.

questions.question: Which is the second most densely populated city in India?
questions.why: Mumbai ranks 1st in population density among Indian cities, Kolkata 2nd — a ranking fact, not just "which city is dense."

questions.question: Who developed the oral polio vaccine?
questions.why: Trap pair — Albert Sabin developed the ORAL (drops) vaccine; Jonas Salk developed the INJECTABLE vaccine. Memory hook: Sabin = Swallow, Salk = Shot. Edward Jenner = smallpox vaccine, Louis Pasteur = rabies/germ theory — both wrong-domain distractors.

questions.question: Which of the following is a festival celebrated by Parsis (Zoroastrians)?
questions.why: FLAGGED — this paper's answer key marks "Zend Avesta," but Zend Avesta is the Zoroastrian holy scripture, not a festival. Navroz (Parsi New Year) is the actual festival among these options. Treat the key as likely wrong here; do not bank "Zend Avesta = festival" as fact. The real fact worth keeping: Navroz = Parsi New Year.
questions.status: stale: key likely erroneous, verify before trusting
questions.attempted: wrong (chose 3, matches this paper's erroneous key) (29 Aug 2026) — taught correct answer is Navroz

questions.question: Who wrote the famous novel 'Anandmath'?
questions.why: Anandmath (1882) contains "Vande Mataram." Don't confuse with Sarat Chandra (Devdas) or Tagore (national anthem, Gitanjali).

questions.question: Who is Dipa Karmakar?
options: The first female Indian gymnast ever to qualify for Olympic Games
The captain of Indian women's cricket team
questions.why: Dipa Karmakar qualified for the Rio 2016 Olympics in gymnastics (Produnova vault), a first for an Indian woman in that sport.

questions.question: Who is the current Chief Election Commissioner of India?
questions.why: Nasim Zaidi was CEC as of 2016. This is a rolling-office fact — the position changes; do not memorise the name, memorise that this is the kind of "current officeholder" question the exam asks, and check the live 2026 name closer to the exam.
questions.practice: Who is the CURRENT (2026) Chief Election Commissioner of India?

questions.question: Who is the current chairperson of Rajya Sabha?
questions.why: Structural fact worth keeping: the Vice President of India is the EX-OFFICIO Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha (always, by constitutional design) — Mohammad Hamid Ansari was VP in 2016. The name is stale; the structural rule (VP = RS Chair) is not.
questions.status: stale: named officeholder changed, but "VP = RS Chairperson" rule is current
questions.practice: Who is the CURRENT (2026) ex-officio Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha (i.e. current VP of India)?
questions.attempted: wrong (chose Jagdeep Dhankhar, a former VP) (29 Aug 2026)

questions.question: Who is the current Secretary-General of the United Nations?
questions.why: Ban Ki-moon was UN SG 2007-2016. Rolling-office fact, verify current 2026 UN SG before the exam.
questions.practice: Who is the CURRENT (2026) UN Secretary-General?

questions.question: Substances like phosphorus burn in air at room temperature without any apparent cause. This type of combustion is called ______.
questions.why: Spontaneous combustion = ignition without an external heat source or spark, purely from the substance's own low ignition point/reactivity. Phosphorus is the classic textbook example.

questions.question: Which of the following nations won the Cricket World Cup 2015?
questions.why: Australia won the 2015 Cricket World Cup (hosted jointly with New Zealand), beating New Zealand in the final. Fixed historical fact, not stale.

questions.question: The Elephanta caves are dedicated to which deity?
questions.why: Elephanta Caves (Mumbai harbour, UNESCO site) are rock-cut temples dedicated to Shiva - the giant Trimurti Sadashiva sculpture is the centerpiece.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the Simlipal bio-reserve located?
questions.why: Simlipal Biosphere Reserve is in Odisha (Mayurbhanj district) - a tiger reserve and UNESCO biosphere reserve.

questions.question: Name a book maintained internationally which keeps a record of all endangered animals and plants. India also maintains one for species found in India.
questions.why: Red Data Book (IUCN) lists threatened/endangered species globally; India maintains its own national Red Data Book.

questions.question: Who is the current Chairman of SEBI?
questions.why: Ajay Tyagi was SEBI Chairman as of Aug 2018 - this is a rolling-office fact, same pattern as CEC/RS Chair/UN SG. The CURRENT (2026) SEBI Chairman is Tuhin Kanta Pandey, who succeeded Madhabi Puri Buch.
questions.status: stale: SEBI Chairman since changed - current (2026) is Tuhin Kanta Pandey

questions.question: Who was the Speaker of the 16th Lok Sabha?
questions.why: Sumitra Mahajan was Speaker of the 16th Lok Sabha (2014-2019). Rolling-office fact - the CURRENT (2026) Lok Sabha Speaker is Om Birla, serving since the 17th Lok Sabha (2019) and continuing into the 18th (2024-present).
questions.status: stale: named Speaker/term changed - current (2026) is Om Birla, 18th Lok Sabha

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the establishment and constitution of the Supreme Court?
questions.why: Article 124 establishes the Supreme Court. Keep a small article-number list: Art 74=aid/advice to President, Art 75=PM appointment, Art 123=President's ordinance power, Art 124=Supreme Court establishment, Art 143=President can consult SC.

questions.question: Which of the following styles of painting belongs to Maharashtra?
questions.why: Warli painting = tribal art from Maharashtra (Warli tribe), simple white geometric figures on mud/red background. Madhubani = Bihar, Kalamkari = Andhra/Telangana - regional art-form pairings are a recurring trap type.

questions.question: What was the rank of India in the World Press Freedom Index 2018?
questions.why: India ranked 138th in the 2018 World Press Freedom Index. This is a yearly-changing statistic - don't memorise the number, memorise that this index exists and roughly what it measures (press freedom by country, published annually by Reporters Without Borders).
questions.status: stale: index rank changes every year, don't memorise the 2018 figure

questions.question: In which state is the Madai festival celebrated?
questions.why: Madai is a tribal harvest/hunting festival celebrated in Chhattisgarh (Bastar region tribes).

questions.question: As per Economic Survey 2017-18, the service sector contributed ______ to India's GVA in 2017-18.
questions.why: Services sector is the largest contributor to India's GVA/GDP, over half - a broad structural fact worth keeping (services > industry > agriculture in India's GVA mix) even though the exact percentage shifts yearly.
questions.status: stale: exact percent is year-specific, but 'services = largest GVA share' is a durable structural fact

questions.question: The President has the power to promulgate ordinances under ______ of the Constitution.
questions.why: Article 123 = President's ordinance-making power when Parliament isn't in session. Pairs with Article 124 (SC establishment) and Article 143 (President can consult SC) as a mini article-number cluster to memorise together.

questions.question: With whom did the Government of India enter a flexible financing agreement to accelerate biopharmaceutical research under the National Biopharma Mission?
questions.why: World Bank financing for the National Biopharma Mission (2017), a scheme to boost India's vaccine/biopharma R&D. Niche scheme-name fact, lower priority than structural/recurring patterns.

questions.question: Indu Malhotra recently became the ______ woman lawyer to be directly elevated from the Bar to the Supreme Court as a judge.
questions.why: Indu Malhotra (2018) was the first woman lawyer directly elevated from the Bar (as opposed to promoted from a High Court) to the Supreme Court. A 'first' fact - these tend to stay permanently true even as time passes, unlike rolling officeholder facts.

questions.question: Which hockey player won the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna award in 2017?
questions.why: Sardara Singh, Indian men's hockey captain, won Khel Ratna in 2017. Fixed historical award-year fact.

questions.question: How many Fundamental Duties are provided by Article 51A of the Constitution?
questions.why: Article 51A lists 11 Fundamental Duties (added by the 42nd Amendment 1976, one more added later by the 86th Amendment in 2002 for parents to educate children 6-14 - total is 11). Compare/contrast with Fundamental RIGHTS (originally 7, now 6 after Right to Property was removed) - don't mix duty-count with rights-count.

questions.question: It takes ____ full grown trees to make one tonne of paper.
questions.why: Standard environmental-science trivia figure: ~17 trees per tonne of paper. Appears across many GK banks as a fixed fact.

questions.question: Who introduced the 'Doctrine of Lapse'?
questions.why: Lord Dalhousie introduced the Doctrine of Lapse (annexation policy for princely states without a natural heir) - a major cause of resentment leading to the 1857 revolt. Distinguish from Lord Canning (Governor-General DURING 1857, ended Doctrine of Lapse afterward) - commonly confused pair since both are mid-1800s Governors-General.

questions.question: Which is the basic unit of inheritance in living organisms that controls transfer of hereditary characteristics from parents to offspring?
questions.why: Gene = basic functional unit of heredity. Chromosome = structure that carries/organizes many genes (made of DNA). Order of scale: Cell > Chromosome > DNA > Gene (a gene is a segment of DNA).

questions.question: World War II began with German invasion of which country?
questions.why: Germany invaded Poland on 1 Sept 1939, triggering WWII (Britain/France declared war days later). Germany invaded Russia (USSR) later, in 1941 - Operation Barbarossa - a different, later event; don't conflate the two invasions.

questions.question: On 15 February 2013, the Chelyabinsk Meteor hit which country?
questions.why: Chelyabinsk meteor airburst over Russia (Feb 2013) - a genuinely fixed historical event, not a rolling fact, safe to keep memorised as-is.

questions.question: Who won the FIDE World Rapid Chess Championship title in 2015?
questions.why: Magnus Carlsen won the 2015 FIDE World Rapid Chess title. This is a year-specific championship result - treat as fixed historical fact (2015 champion), don't confuse with 'who is current champion' which changes yearly.
questions.status: current: fixed to year 2015, but don't assume Carlsen is still current champion in 2026 without checking

questions.question: The Washington Accord is an international accreditation agreement for educational degrees in which field?
questions.why: Washington Accord = mutual recognition agreement for accredited ENGINEERING degree programs across member countries (India joined via NBA).

questions.question: In India, inflation is measured by:
options: Consumer price index for urban non-manual workers
Consumer price index for agricultural workers
questions.why: FLAG - verify before trusting. India shifted its OFFICIAL headline inflation benchmark from WPI to CPI (Consumer Price Index, combined rural+urban) around 2014-15, under RBI's inflation-targeting framework. This paper's answer (WPI) reflects the older policy; the current (2026) primary inflation gauge for monetary policy is CPI, not WPI. Don't bank WPI as 'the' answer blind.
questions.status: stale: official inflation benchmark shifted from WPI to CPI post-2014

questions.question: National income is defined as:
options: Net National Product at Market price
Net National Product at factor cost
Net Domestic Product at market price
Net Domestic Product at factor cost
questions.why: National Income (standard definition) = Net National Product at FACTOR COST (i.e., NNP minus indirect taxes plus subsidies - the value actually received by factors of production). Distinguish Market Price (includes taxes) vs Factor Cost (excludes taxes, the 'true' income to producers), and National (includes net income from abroad) vs Domestic (excludes it).

questions.question: Organisms that generate energy using light are called:
questions.why: Photoautotrophs = use light (photo) to make their own food (auto = self, troph = feeding), e.g. plants, algae, cyanobacteria - basic photosynthesis vocabulary.

questions.question: Which technique is used for the study of land use pattern?
questions.why: Modern land-use studies combine all three: satellite imaging (capture), GIS (analysis/mapping layers), GPS (ground-truthing/positioning) - the 'most complete' answer wins when an option stacks multiple correct techniques together.

questions.question: Soil particle sizes (clay/silt/sand/boulder) in nature follow which statistical distribution?
questions.why: Niche geology/soil-science fact - low priority to memorise deeply, flagging as seen but not worth drilling given its narrow applicability.

questions.question: Which of the following latitudes passes through India?
questions.why: Tropic of Cancer (23.5N) passes through India (through 8 states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, WB, Tripura, Mizoram). The Equator, Arctic Circle, and Tropic of Capricorn do NOT pass through India - only the Tropic of Cancer does.

questions.question: ______ is the phenomenon of a species moving from its own habitat to another habitat for a period each year for a specific purpose like breeding.
questions.why: Migration = periodic, purposeful movement (e.g. breeding, feeding). Distinguish from Hibernation (staying put, dormant state through winter) and Adaptation (a trait change over generations, not a yearly movement).

questions.question: What was India's rank in the FDI Confidence Index 2018 released by AT Kearney?
questions.why: India ranked 11th in AT Kearney's 2018 FDI Confidence Index. Yearly-changing ranking stat - same caution as the Press Freedom Index question, don't memorise the number as permanent.
questions.status: stale: index rank changes yearly, don't memorise the 2018 figure

questions.question: Census 2011 was the ______ census of its kind conducted in India since 1872.
questions.why: India's census series started 1872 (under British rule); 2011 was the 15th census overall and the 7th after independence (independent India's censuses started 1951). Note: the next census (due 2021) was postponed and still hasn't happened as of 2026, so 2011 remains the most recent official census.

questions.question: What is a saline lake separated from the sea by a sand bar/narrow strip of sand called?
questions.why: Lagoon = shallow saltwater body separated from the open sea by a sandbar/reef/barrier island (e.g. Chilika Lake, Odisha - India's largest lagoon). Estuary = where a river meets the sea (freshwater/saltwater mix), a different landform entirely - common confusion pair.

questions.question: How many self-help groups of tribal gatherers were constituted under the Van Dhan Yojana (as reported in this paper)?
questions.why: Van Dhan Yojana = scheme for tribal minor-forest-produce value addition via self-help groups. Very niche, rapidly outdated scheme statistic - low priority, don't drill the number, just recognise the scheme name/purpose if it comes up.
questions.status: stale: scheme statistic long outdated, scheme itself may have expanded significantly since

questions.question: Who started the newspaper 'Sambad Kaumudi'?
questions.why: Raja Ram Mohan Roy - social reformer (fought Sati, founded Brahmo Samaj) - started Sambad Kaumudi (1821), an early Bengali-language reformist newspaper.

questions.question: The Bagh style of textile art printing belongs to which state?
questions.why: Bagh print = hand block-printed textile art from Bagh, Madhya Pradesh, using natural dyes. Another state-craft pairing to add to the Warli(Maharashtra)/Madhubani(Bihar)/Kalamkari(Andhra) list.

questions.question: According to Article 143 of the Constitution, who has the power to consult the Supreme Court?
questions.why: Article 143 = President's power to seek the Supreme Court's advisory opinion on questions of law/fact. Third article in the mini-cluster with Article 123 (ordinance power) and Article 124 (SC establishment).

questions.question: As per Economic Survey 2017-18, the average decline in Kharif-season rainfall between the 1970s and 2000s was:
questions.why: Niche year-specific statistic from one Economic Survey edition - low priority, the durable takeaway is simply 'Kharif rainfall has trended down over decades,' not the exact mm figure.
questions.status: stale: specific figure tied to one Economic Survey edition

questions.question: Which team won the Indian Premier League (IPL) 2018 title?
questions.why: Chennai Super Kings won IPL 2018 (their 3rd title, first after returning from a 2-year suspension). Fixed historical fact per year - IPL winner changes annually, so if asked for 'current' champion, verify the latest season instead.
questions.status: current: fixed to year 2018, verify latest season separately if asked for 'current' IPL champion

questions.question: How many classical dance forms are officially recognised in India?
questions.why: 8 classical dances: Bharatanatyam (TN), Kathak (UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Odissi (Odisha), Kuchipudi (Andhra), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam). Everything else (Bhangra, Garba, Ghoomar, Bihu) is folk, not classical.

questions.question: Which of the following is a FOLK dance, not a classical one?
questions.why: Bhangra (Punjab) is folk. The other three are among India's 8 officially recognised classical dance forms. Exam trap: mixing one folk name into a list of classical names.

questions.question: Zakir Hussain is a renowned maestro of which instrument?
questions.why: Zakir Hussain = Tabla. Extends the instrument-maestro pairing list: Sitar-Ravi Shankar, Sarod-Amjad Ali Khan, Santoor-Shivkumar Sharma, Flute-Hariprasad Chaurasia, Shehnai-Bismillah Khan, Tabla-Zakir Hussain, Violin-L. Subramaniam.

questions.question: L. Subramaniam is a maestro of which instrument?
questions.why: L. Subramaniam = Violin (Carnatic tradition). Same pairing-list pattern as Zakir Hussain/Tabla — memorise the list as a set, not one name at a time.

questions.question: Which term denotes a batsman dismissed without scoring any run in cricket?
questions.why: 'Duck' = dismissed for 0 runs (duck egg is 0-shaped). 'Golden duck' = out on the very first ball faced. Don't confuse with 'maiden' (an over with no runs scored, a bowling term, not batting).

questions.question: In tennis, a score of zero is called:
questions.why: 'Love' = zero in tennis (from French l'oeuf = egg, shaped like 0 — same root idea as cricket's 'duck' for 0, different sport, different word).

questions.question: In chess, a position where the king is NOT in check but has no legal move, resulting in a draw, is called:
questions.why: Stalemate = no legal move, king safe = DRAW. Checkmate = king IS in check, no escape = one side WINS. The two terms are opposites in outcome despite sounding similar — a classic confusion pair.

questions.question: The five Olympic rings represent:
questions.why: The 5 interlocking rings (blue, yellow, black, green, red) represent the 5 inhabited continents of the world (Americas counted as one) — not any specific countries, sports, or cities.

questions.question: Which is India's highest civilian award?
questions.why: Bharat Ratna sits above all Padma awards. Full descending order: Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri. Khel Ratna is a separate, sport-specific highest honour, not part of this civilian-award ladder.

questions.question: In the Padma awards, which rank comes immediately after Padma Vibhushan?
questions.why: Order: Padma Vibhushan (2nd highest civilian award overall) > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri. Bharat Ratna is ABOVE Padma Vibhushan, not below it — a common ordering trap. Ashoka Chakra is a gallantry award, different category entirely (peacetime bravery, not civilian merit).

questions.question: Who was the first Indian (and first Asian) Nobel laureate?
questions.why: Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 — first Indian AND first Asian Nobel laureate. C.V. Raman (Physics, 1930) was the first Indian science laureate, a different 'first' — don't conflate the two.

questions.question: Which Nobel Prize category was added in 1969 and was NOT part of Alfred Nobel's original 1895 will?
questions.why: Economics (formally 'The Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel') was added in 1969 by Sweden's central bank — technically not an original Nobel Prize category, though popularly called one. The original 5 (Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature, Peace) were all in Nobel's 1895 will.

questions.question: Who wrote 'Gitanjali'?
questions.why: Gitanjali (Song Offerings) by Tagore won him the 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature. He also wrote India's national anthem (Jana Gana Mana) — don't confuse with Bankim Chandra, who wrote Anandmath/Vande Mataram.

questions.question: 'My Experiments with Truth' is the autobiography of:
questions.why: Gandhi's autobiography. Distinguish from Nehru's 'The Discovery of India' (written in prison, a history/reflection book, not an autobiography).

questions.question: Who wrote the novel 'Godan'?
questions.why: Godan (The Gift of a Cow) by Munshi Premchand, a major Hindi novelist. R.K. Narayan wrote 'Malgudi Days' (English, fictional South Indian town) — different author, different language, different era-flavour, commonly mixed up in author-matching questions.

questions.question: India's national aquatic animal is:
questions.why: Ganges River Dolphin — endangered, freshwater-only dolphin species. Part of the national-symbols set worth memorising as a group: bird=Peacock, animal=Tiger, flower=Lotus, tree=Banyan, aquatic animal=Ganges River Dolphin.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian to travel to space?
questions.why: Rakesh Sharma (1984, aboard a Soviet Soyuz mission) — first Indian in space. Kalpana Chawla was the first Indian-born WOMAN in space (but flying as a US/NASA astronaut, and a different 'first' entirely) — a very common confusion pair, keep them distinct.

questions.question: Who was India's first woman President?
questions.why: Pratibha Patil (2007-2012) was India's first woman President. Indira Gandhi was the first woman PRIME MINISTER — a completely different office, frequently confused because both are 'first woman in a top job.' Droupadi Murmu is a later, more recent woman President, not the first.

questions.question: Which latitude line passes through India, making it the correct reference for questions about India's latitudinal position?
questions.why: Tropic of Cancer (23.5 degrees N) is the only one of these four latitudes that passes through India, cutting across 8 states. Already banked from the ATC 2015 paper (Q173) — repeating here as a static fact worth its own standalone recall, not just a paper-specific answer.

questions.question: India's highest peak (fully within Indian territory) is:
questions.why: Kangchenjunga (Sikkim/Nepal border) is the highest peak entirely within India. Mount Everest is in Nepal (not India). K2 is in Pakistan-administered Gilgit-Baltistan (India claims the broader region but does not control it) — both are common wrong picks for 'India's highest peak.'

questions.question: Select the related letters from the given alternatives. FHJL : USQO :: PRTV : ?
questions.why: This is an alphabet-MIRROR pair, not a constant shift — pair letters equidistant from A and Z using mirror(n) = 27-n (A<->Z, B<->Y, C<->X...). Check: F(6)->27-6=21=U, H(8)->19=S, J(10)->17=Q, L(12)->15=O — every letter of FHJL mirrors exactly to USQO. Apply the same mirror to PRTV: P(16)->11=K, R(18)->9=I, T(20)->7=G, V(22)->5=E = KIGE. Trap: the first pair's shifts (+15,+11,+7,+3) look like a pattern if you only check letter-to-letter differences — but that shift sequence does NOT reapply correctly to the second group. Whenever a shift isn't constant across all four letters, test the mirror-pair rule before anything else.
questions.attempted: correct (7 Sep 2026, after one self-correction from a shift-based first attempt)

questions.question: Select the related numbers from the given alternatives. 23 : 34 :: 47 : ?
questions.why: This looks like an A:B::C:D analogy (find the B-A rule, apply to C) but that reading has no clean answer. The real trick: 23, 34, 47 are actually three consecutive terms of ONE hidden series, and the difference between terms increases by a constant: 34-23=11, 47-34=13 (differences rising by 2), so the next difference is 15 and 47+15=62. Trap: whenever an "analogy" pair's rule refuses to reapply cleanly to the third number, check whether all the given numbers are secretly one running series instead of two independent pairs.

questions.question: Select the one which is different from other three alternatives.
questions.why: Assign:Allot, Vacant:Empty, and Solicit:Request are all SYNONYM pairs (same meaning). Advance:Retreat is an ANTONYM pair (opposite meaning) — that's the odd one out. Trap: always classify each pair's relationship type first (synonym/antonym/part-whole/etc) before comparing options; picking based on "meaning similarity" alone without naming the relationship type causes slips.

questions.question: Select the one which is different from other three alternatives.
questions.why: In 27:72, 38:83, and 45:54, the second number is the exact digit-reversal of the first (27 reversed = 72, 38 reversed = 83, 45 reversed = 54). 56:68 breaks this — reverse of 56 is 65, not 68. That's the odd one out. Trap: with number-pair classification, always test digit-reversal and digit-sum/difference patterns before assuming there's no numeric relationship.

questions.question: Choose the correct alternative from the given ones which will complete the series. BMX, EOW, HQV, ?, NUT
questions.why: Split into three independent letter tracks and find each one's step. 1st letters: B,E,H,?,N step +3 (B->E->H->K->N), so the missing term starts with K. 2nd letters: M,O,Q,?,U step +2 (M->O->Q->S->U), giving S. 3rd letters: X,W,V,?,T step -1 (X->W->V->U->T), giving U. Combined: KSU. Trap: always track each letter POSITION as its own independent series with its own step size and direction (some ascend, some descend) rather than looking for one rule across the whole group.

questions.question: Choose the correct alternative from the given ones which will complete the number series. 6, 11, 20, 37, 70, ?
questions.why: First differences are 5, 9, 17, 33 — each one equals (previous difference x 2) - 1. Next difference = 33x2-1 = 65. 70+65 = 135. Trap: when first differences aren't constant or simply arithmetic, check whether the differences themselves follow a doubling-minus-something rule before giving up on a pattern.

questions.question: Six friends J, K, L, M, N and O are sitting around a circle facing towards the centre. J is not adjacent to K or L; M is not adjacent to L or N; K and L are adjacent. O is in the middle of M and L. If one neighbour of J is M, who is the other one?
questions.why: Build the most tightly forced block FIRST: "O is between M and L" plus "K and L are adjacent" chains into one fixed sequence, M-O-L-K, that must sit together. That leaves only J and N for the two remaining seats between K and M. Since J cannot be adjacent to K (given), J must take the seat next to M, leaving N next to K. Final circle: M-O-L-K-N-J-(back to M). J's neighbours are N and M; given one is M, the other is N. Trap: don't try to place all six people at once — always build the forced block from the strongest linking clues first, then fit the remaining people using the "cannot be adjacent to" restrictions.

questions.question: P is Q's brother; R is P's mother; S is R's father; Q is S's granddaughter. How is Q related to T who is P's son?
questions.why: Draw the family tree, don't hold it in your head. R = mother of both P and Q (P and Q are siblings). S = R's father = grandfather of P and Q. "Q is S's granddaughter" just confirms Q is female. T = P's son, so T's parent is P and T's aunt is P's sister = Q. Answer: Aunt. Trap: multi-generation blood-relation chains fail when solved in your head — draw the tree one relation at a time, resolve the innermost relation first, and only then read off the final answer.

questions.question: From the given alternatives, select the word which can be formed using the letters of the given word. You can use a letter only as many times as it appears in the word below. DISPROPORTIONATE
questions.why: Count each letter's SUPPLY in the source word first: D1,I2,S1,P2,R2,O3,T2,N1,A1,E1. Then check each option against that supply, not just "is the letter present" but "is there ENOUGH of it." PERSONAL needs an L, which doesn't exist at all — fails. DISPOSE needs S twice, source has only 1 S — fails. PROPONENT needs N twice, source has only 1 N — fails. STATION needs S1,T2,A1,I1,O1,N1, all within supply — works. Trap: checking only "is each letter present" and stopping there is the most common mistake; always verify the COUNT of the tightest-supply letter in each option.

questions.question: If in a certain code language PORTER is written as TSVXIV, how would SHOWER be written in that code?
questions.why: Always test a CONSTANT shift on every letter first for coding questions — it's the most common pattern. P(16)->T(20): +4. O(15)->S(19): +4. R(18)->V(22): +4. T(20)->X(24): +4. E(5)->I(9): +4. R(18)->V(22): +4. Every letter shifts by exactly +4. Apply to SHOWER: S->W, H->L, O->S, W->A, E->I, R->V = WLSAIV. Trap: don't jump to position-dependent or reversal-based coding rules before ruling out a simple constant shift across every letter.

questions.question: Some equations are solved on the basis of a certain system. Find the correct answer for the unsolved equation on that basis. 452 = 45, 371 = 59, 253 = ?
questions.why: Test SUM OF SQUARES OF THE DIGITS first for any digit-equation coding puzzle — it's a very common CBT trick. 4^2+5^2+2^2 = 16+25+4 = 45 (matches). 3^2+7^2+1^2 = 9+49+1 = 59 (matches). So 2^2+5^2+3^2 = 4+25+9 = 38. Trap: the first pair's result (45) happens to also look like just "the first two digits of 452" — a coincidence that only fits ONE of the two given equations. Always verify a candidate rule against BOTH given equations before applying it to the unknown, never just one.
questions.attempted: correct (7 Sep 2026, both the original and the fresh modelled retest)

questions.question: Mukesh walked 20 metres towards South. Then he turned to his left and walked 10 metres. He then turned to his left and walked 20 metres. He again turned to his right and walked 7 metres. At what distance and in which direction is Mukesh from the starting point?
questions.why: Track facing direction and (x,y) position as two SEPARATE variables, updating one step at a time. Start (0,0) facing South -> walk 20 South -> (0,-20). Turn left (South->East) -> walk 10 East -> (10,-20). Turn left again (East->North) -> walk 20 North -> (10,0). Turn right (North->East) -> walk 7 East -> (17,0). Final position (17,0) vs start (0,0) = 17 metres East. Trap: the riskiest step is usually the LAST turn, not the first — people get the direction-after-turn wrong more often once several turns have already happened and they lose track of current facing.

questions.question: Consider the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Statements: (i) All fruits are flowers. (ii) No flowers are leaves. Conclusions: I. No fruits are leaves. II. All flowers are fruits.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I and II follow
questions.why: Fruits are a SUBSET of flowers (All A are B), and flowers never touch leaves (No B are C) — so fruits, sitting entirely inside flowers, can never touch leaves either: No fruits are leaves (I) FOLLOWS validly. Conclusion II reverses the direction of the first statement (fruits subset of flowers does NOT mean flowers subset of fruits) — II does NOT follow. Trap: "All A are B" never implies "All B are A" — reversing a universal statement's direction is the single most common syllogism trap.

questions.question: What is the smallest 4-digit number which is divisible by 18, 24 and 32?
questions.why: Find LCM(18,24,32) first: 18=2x3^2, 24=2^3x3, 32=2^5, so LCM=2^5x3^2=288. Smallest 4-digit multiple of 288: 1000/288=3.47, so the next multiple is 4x288=1152. Trap: "smallest number divisible by all of these" always means LCM, not HCF — the reverse question ("largest measure that divides all exactly") is HCF (see Q220).

questions.question: Two containers contain 850 litres and 680 litres of oil respectively. What is the maximum capacity of a container which can measure the oil of both containers an exact number of times?
questions.why: HCF(850,680): 850=2x5^2x17, 680=2^3x5x17, HCF=2x5x17=170. Trap: "maximum size that measures both exactly" is always HCF (biggest common factor), the opposite direction from "smallest number divisible by all" (LCM, see Q219) — read which direction the question asks before picking.

questions.question: Both x and y vary directly with each other and when x=20, y=28. Which of the following is not a possible pair of corresponding values?
questions.why: The fixed ratio is y:x=28:20=7:5. Check each pair's ratio (second:first): 25:35 -> 35/25=7/5 valid. 35:25 -> 25/35=5/7 INVALID (inverted). 35:49 -> 49/35=7/5 valid. 15:21 -> 21/15=7/5 valid. Trap: in direct-proportion odd-one-out questions, compute the ratio in the SAME order (second value / first value) for every pair — an inverted pair is the easiest way examiners hide the odd one out.

questions.question: If a:b = 5:7, b:c = 2:3, what is the value of c:a?
questions.why: Make the shared term (b) equal in both ratios using their LCM: b is 7 in the first ratio and 2 in the second, LCM(7,2)=14. Scale a:b=5:7 by x2 -> a:b=10:14. Scale b:c=2:3 by x7 -> b:c=14:21. Now b matches (14) in both: a:b:c=10:14:21, so c:a=21:10. Trap: never try to combine two ratios directly without first making their shared term equal — that IS the method, skipping it is the only way to get this wrong.

questions.question: If Rs. 600 become Rs.720 in 4 years, then what is the rate of simple interest per annum?
questions.why: Interest earned = 720-600=120. SI formula: I = P x R x T / 100, so 120 = 600 x R x 4 / 100 = 24R, giving R=120/24=5%. Standard SI plug-in, no trick.

questions.question: A sum of 10,000 is invested at the rate of 8% per year for 12 months. What is Compound interest if interest is compounded half-yearly?
questions.why: Whenever compounding isn't yearly, convert BOTH the rate and the time to match the compounding period: half-yearly rate = 8/2=4%, number of half-year periods in 12 months = 2. CI = 10000x(1.04)^2 - 10000 = 10000x1.0816 - 10000 = 816. Trap: never apply the annual rate directly to the annual time when the compounding period isn't yearly — always halve/quarter the rate and double/quadruple the periods to match.

questions.question: Rekha offers a discount of 10% on mark price an article and still makes a profit of 25%. If cost price of article is Rs. 360, what is mark price of the article?
questions.why: SP = CP x 1.25 = 360 x 1.25 = 450 (from the profit). SP is also MP x 0.9 (after the 10% discount), so MP = SP / 0.9 = 450 / 0.9 = 500. Trap: build SP from the profit% on CP first, then work backward through the discount% to reach MP — don't try to combine discount% and profit% into one single percentage shortcut, it doesn't work that way.

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 30 km/h and speed of stream is 6 km/h. What is the time taken by the boat in minutes to cover a distance of 12 km?
questions.why: Downstream speed = boat speed + stream speed (the current helps) = 30+6=36 km/h. Time = 12/36 hr = 1/3 hr = 20 minutes. Trap: downstream always ADDS the stream speed, upstream always SUBTRACTS it (current works against you) — check the direction stated before picking the formula.

questions.question: The fourth term of an A.P. is 3 and 12th term is -13. What is the sum of the first 10 terms of the A.P.?
questions.why: a+3d=3 and a+11d=-13. Subtracting: 8d=-16, d=-2, so a=3-3(-2)=9. Sum of first n terms = n/2 x (2a+(n-1)d): S10 = 5 x (18+9x(-2)) = 5 x (18-18) = 0. Standard two-equations-two-unknowns AP setup, no trick.

questions.question: Arun can finish a work in 36 hours and Ballu is twice as efficient as Arun. If they work together, how many hours they will take to finish the same work?
questions.why: Twice as efficient means half the time: Ballu finishes in 18 hours. Combined rate = 1/36 + 1/18 = 1/36 + 2/36 = 3/36 = 1/12, so combined time = 12 hours. Standard efficiency-ratio time-and-work, no trick.

questions.topic: Heights and distances (angle of elevation, two points)
questions.question: The angle of elevation of a 30 m high tower from two point on the ground are 30 degrees and 45 degrees respectively. If both points and base of the tower are in a line, the distance between two points is:
questions.why: From the 45-degree point (closer to the tower): distance = 30/tan(45) = 30m. From the 30-degree point (farther): distance = 30/tan(30) = 30sqrt(3)m. Distance BETWEEN the two points = 30sqrt(3) - 30 = 30(sqrt(3)-1)m. Trap: the SMALLER angle of elevation always belongs to the FARTHER point — draw the triangle with both points on the same side of the tower before computing, don't just plug numbers into a formula.

questions.question: What are the values of k for which the equation 4x^2 - kx + 9 = 0 has real roots?
options: 12<=k<=-12 (paper's non-standard notation for the union of two rays)
questions.why: Real roots require discriminant >= 0: k^2 - 4(4)(9) >= 0, so k^2 >= 144, giving k<=-12 OR k>=12. The paper's marked option "12<=k<=-12" is not a valid interval read literally (12 is not less than -12) — it appears to be sloppy shorthand attempting to express the union of the two rays (k<=-12 or k>=12), not a real interval. The reusable rule to keep is the discriminant condition itself (D>=0 for real roots), not this option's confusing notation.
questions.status: current (rule verified independently; option notation flagged as confusing, not the underlying math)

questions.question: Select the word that will fill in the blank correctly. 'If you are focused, you can ________ your goals', her coach said.
questions.why: After a modal verb (can, will, should, must...), the following verb is always the bare infinitive — no -s, no -ing, no -ed. Trap: this rule holds regardless of the subject's number or the surrounding tense; modals never take a conjugated verb after them.

questions.question: Find the error in the following sentence. I don't like to invests in stock markets as a fall in the market can take you by surprise.
questions.why: After "to" (infinitive marker), the verb must stay in base form — "to invest," not "to invests." Trap: spot-the-error questions on infinitives are easy to miss because the -s looks like normal present-tense agreement; check specifically whether the verb follows "to" before applying subject-verb agreement rules.

questions.question: Find the error in the following sentence. I saw a lot of rubble and debris dumped by the hillside and was worried about its effective on the environment.
options: I saw a lot of rubble and debris
and was worried about its effective
questions.why: "Effective" is an adjective used where a noun is needed — "its effect" (the impact/result), not "its effective." Trap: spot-the-error questions frequently hide a wrong part of speech (adjective used as a noun, or vice versa) rather than a tense or agreement mistake — always check whether each word's part of speech fits its grammatical slot.

questions.question: Select the correct synonym of the underlined word. The serenity of the lake was immense and urged me to stay an extra day at the resort.
questions.why: Serenity means peacefulness/calmness of a place or state of mind. "Scenic beauty" describes appearance, not the feeling of calm — a common near-miss distractor in synonym questions. Trap: pick the option matching the PRECISE shade of meaning, not just the general topic area (a lake can have both scenic beauty and serenity, but the word itself only means the latter).

questions.question: Select the correct synonym of the underlined word. It was shocking to note how the facts were distorted by the President of the Association when he presented the annual report.
questions.why: Distorted means deliberately twisted/bent out of true shape — closest match is misrepresented (deliberately presented wrongly). Misjudged/misinterpreted imply an honest wrong understanding, not deliberate twisting — a subtle but important distinction. Trap: several "mis-" prefixed options can look interchangeable; separate deliberate distortion from honest error before choosing.

questions.question: Select the correct antonym of the underlined word. I tried to forego the chance to show my leadership skills to my teacher so that my friend, who was always helpful, could get a chance to be the class monitor for this month.
questions.why: Forego means to give up or decline something voluntarily. Its opposite is to seize/take it instead — grab. "Let go" and "escape" are near-synonyms of forego, not antonyms — a classic antonym-question trap where a synonym is placed among the options to catch a rushed reader. Trap: always confirm the underlined word's exact meaning first, then scan specifically for options that are synonyms in disguise before picking the true opposite.

questions.question: Select the correct antonym of the underlined word. Those who lead sedentary lives are warned of the consequences by their doctors but they do not pay heed at all.
questions.why: Sedentary means characterized by sitting/inactivity. Its opposite is active. "Lazy" and "sluggish" are near-synonyms of sedentary (both describe low activity/energy), not antonyms — same synonym-in-disguise trap as Q238. Trap: when 3 of 4 antonym options all sit on the same side of the meaning spectrum, the odd one out (truly opposite) is usually the answer.

questions.question: Select the word that is spelt CORRECTLY.
questions.why: Correct spellings are enchantment, engagement, installment, ingredient — only "installment" among the given options is already correctly spelt. Trap: the "in-" vs "en-" prefix mix-up is a very common Indian-English spelling error; when unsure, sound out whether the word should start with "en-" (most do) rather than defaulting to "in-".

questions.question: Select the alternative that gives the correct meaning of the underlined idiom/phrase. At the annual conference, it was decided to go back to the drawing board as the product had failed in the market.
options: evolve a new plan to stop losses
study the impact on the market
questions.why: "Go back to the drawing board" means to start completely over from scratch after a failure, not to make incremental fixes. Trap: idioms cannot be derived literally from their individual words ("drawing board" has nothing to do with art/design here) — they must be recognized as fixed phrases with memorized meanings.

questions.question: Select the alternative that gives the correct meaning of the underlined idiom/phrase. I was taken to task by my boss for my shoddy presentation.
questions.why: "Taken to task" means scolded/reprimanded for a mistake. Trap: "motivated" and "praised" are the opposite emotional tone from the idiom's actual meaning — a rushed reader might associate "boss talking to me" with something positive; always confirm the idiom's fixed meaning rather than guessing from surrounding tone.

questions.question: Select the word that will fill in the blank correctly. "I ________ in life after death. Do you?" the hand-reading expert asked me.
questions.why: Needs first-person present tense matching subject "I" with the correct verb meaning "to have faith in": believe. "Bely" is not a real word (distractor), "betray" and "balance" are real words but wrong meaning entirely. Trap: fill-in-the-blank vocabulary questions sometimes include a fake/misspelt word as a distractor — check that each option is even a real word before checking meaning.

questions.question: Fill in the blanks with appropriate words. Sushmita is allergic ________ almonds. Whenever she eats them, she develops a rash on her body.
questions.why: "Allergic TO" is a fixed collocation — prepositions after specific adjectives (allergic to, afraid of, good at, interested in) are memorized pairs, not logically derivable. Trap: don't try to reason out the preposition from general logic; build a mental list of fixed adjective-preposition pairs instead.

questions.question: Select the correct voice form that will fill in the blank correctly. After the Rio Olympics girls who are participating in sporting events ________________ with a lot of respect.
questions.why: Present-continuous PASSIVE with a plural subject ("girls") always takes the form "are being + past participle": are being treated. "Was treating" and "is treating" are active voice (wrong voice entirely), "have being shown" is a garbled non-standard form. Trap: check subject number, voice, AND tense together as one combined form — not one at a time — since passive continuous has a single fixed shape (am/is/are + being + past participle).

questions.question: Select the correct voice form that will fill in the blank correctly. Efforts ________________ to ensure free quality education to all the children in the country but there are many pitfalls in the system.
questions.why: Same rule as Q245 — plural subject ("Efforts") + present continuous passive = "are being + past participle": are being made. "Has been making" is active present-perfect-continuous (wrong voice), "is being made"/"is doing" use singular "is" with a plural subject (agreement error). Trap: identical passive-continuous-with-plural-subject pattern as the previous question — once you spot "are being + past participle" as the fixed shape, apply it directly.

questions.topic: Para jumble (sentence ordering via cause-effect chain)
questions.question: Read the passage and arrange the sentences B to E in the correct order. A comes first, F comes last. A: During the Monsoons the sky is overcast with dark clouds. B: After the strong winds it starts drizzling. C: Before dark clouds appear in the sky you can see a breeze blowing gently. D: The breeze soon becomes a strong gust of wind. E: And soon the drizzle becomes more intense and there is light rain. F: Light rain is usually followed by heavy rains.
questions.why: Trace the actual physical/time sequence being described using explicit linking words: C ("before dark clouds appear, breeze blows gently") -> D ("the breeze SOON becomes a strong gust") -> B ("AFTER the strong winds it starts drizzling") -> E ("SOON the drizzle becomes more intense"). Order: C-D-B-E. Trap: para-jumble questions need you to follow words like "after," "soon," "before" that explicitly chain one sentence to the next — don't order sentences by surface topic similarity alone, follow the explicit sequence markers.

questions.question: A subway train starts from rest at a station and accelerates at a rate of 2ms^-2 for 10s. It then runs at a constant speed for 30s and deaccelerates at 4ms^-2 until it stops at the next station. The distance between the two stations is:
questions.why: Break into three phases. Phase 1 (accelerate 0→v at 2m/s² for 10s): v=20m/s, distance=½·2·10²=100m. Phase 2 (constant 20m/s for 30s): 600m. Phase 3 (decelerate 20→0 at 4m/s²): t=v/a=5s, distance=v²/(2a)=400/8=50m. Total=100+600+50=750m. This is Class XI kinematics (currently "Learning" in STUDY_PROGRESS, not yet Solid) — the reusable method is splitting any multi-phase motion into separate v-t triangles/rectangles and summing areas.

questions.question: Which of the following quantities is a vector?
questions.why: Area can be treated as a vector (magnitude = extent, direction = the outward normal to the surface) — this convention matters in flux integrals (Gauss's law, etc.). Volume, plane angle, and speed are all scalars (magnitude only, no meaningful direction).

questions.question: If the universal gravitational constant were decreasing with time, then satellite in orbit would still maintain its:
questions.why: Gravity is a central force (always points toward Earth's centre), so it exerts zero torque about that centre regardless of its strength — angular momentum (L = mvr) is conserved as long as the force stays central, even if G itself changes. Orbital radius, speed, and period would all have to adjust as G changes to keep the orbit consistent, but L stays fixed.

questions.question: The velocity with which a projectile must be fired so that it escapes earth's gravitation does not depend on:
questions.why: Escape velocity v = sqrt(2GM/R) — derived from energy conservation where the projectile's own mass cancels out of both the kinetic and potential energy terms. So it depends on Earth's mass M, Earth's radius R, and G, but never on the mass of the thing being launched.

questions.question: The second law of thermodynamics introduces the concept of:
questions.why: The zeroth law introduces temperature, the first law introduces internal energy, and the second law is the one that introduces entropy (a measure of disorder/energy unavailable to do work) — it states entropy of an isolated system never decreases.

questions.question: The manifestation of band structure in solids is a consequence of
questions.why: Pauli's exclusion principle forbids two electrons from occupying the same quantum state; when atoms pack into a solid, their discrete atomic energy levels must split apart into a near-continuum of closely-spaced allowed levels (bands) to accommodate every electron without violating exclusion.

questions.question: A disc shaped magnet levitates above a superconducting material that has been cooled by liquid nitrogen. This happens because a superconductor is:
questions.why: A superconductor expels magnetic field lines from its interior (the Meissner effect) — it behaves as a perfect diamagnet (χ = -1), which repels the magnet's field and produces the levitation.

questions.question: An ideal gas engine operates in a Carnot cycle. It absorbs heat at a temperature T1 and exhausts heat at T2. The efficiency of this engine is:
questions.why: Standard formula, worth memorising cold: η = (T1-T2)/T1 = 1 - T2/T1, where T1 is the hot reservoir and T2 the cold sink (both in Kelvin). Trap: don't divide by T2 or add the temperatures — only this exact ratio is the Carnot efficiency.

questions.question: Superposition of two wave trains of same amplitudes and nearly same frequencies, moving in the same direction, results in the formation of beats. The maximum loudness heard at the waxing is n times the loudness of each of the component wave trains. The value of n is:
questions.why: At the loudest point of a beat, the two equal-amplitude waves add constructively, so the resultant amplitude is 2A (double each wave's amplitude A). Since loudness/intensity is proportional to amplitude squared, intensity there = (2A)²/A² = 4 times a single wave's loudness. Trap: doubling amplitude quadruples intensity, not doubles it — this is the same amplitude-vs-intensity trap as any wave interference question.

questions.question: An earthquake generates both transverse (S) and longitudinal (P) waves in earth. The speed of S waves is about 4.5kms^-1 and that of P wave 8.0kms^-1. A seismograph records P and S waves from an earthquake. The first P wave arrives 4.0 min before the first S wave. The epicenter is located at a distance of about:
questions.why: Time for each wave to cover distance d: t_P=d/8.0, t_S=d/4.5. Their difference equals the given 4.0 min (240s): d(1/4.5 - 1/8.0)=240 → d×0.0972=240 → d≈2469 km, which rounds to the "about 2500 km" option. Note: unlike the similar-looking flagged item elsewhere in this project (a different paper's Q9, where "4.0 min" only works if read as "4.0 ms"), THIS question's numbers check out correctly as printed — verified independently, no flag needed here.

questions.question: Quantization of electric charge is demonstrated by:
questions.why: Millikan's oil-drop experiment measured the charge on individual oil droplets and found every value was an integer multiple of a smallest unit (e) — direct evidence charge comes in discrete quanta, not a continuum.

questions.question: Ampere's circuital law can be expressed as:
questions.why: Ampere's law in differential form: curl of B equals μ times the current density J — magnetic fields curl around currents. (Div B = 0 is a different Maxwell equation, expressing no magnetic monopoles.)

questions.topic: Electric field of an infinite charged wire (Gauss's law)
questions.question: According to Gauss's law, the electric field due to an infinitely long thin charged wire varies as:
questions.why: Applying Gauss's law with a cylindrical surface around the wire, the field spreads over a cylinder's curved area (∝r), so E∝1/r — a slower fall-off than a point charge's 1/r² because the "spreading surface" grows only linearly with distance for a line source, not with the square.

questions.topic: Force between a current loop and a parallel wire
questions.question: A rectangular loop of sides 15cm and 10cm, carrying a current of 1A, is placed with its longer side parallel to a long straight wire carrying a current of 2A placed at a distance of 2cm. The net force experienced by the loop is:
options: 25×10^-7 N away from the longer side
30×10^-7 N away from the longer side
questions.why: Each long side of the loop feels a force from the wire's field (F=μ0·I1·I2·L/(2π·d)) — the near side (2cm away) and far side (2+10=12cm away) get unequal forces since force falls off with distance, and the two currents run parallel (attracting) so the net force pulls the loop toward the wire, i.e. "towards the longer side." The 25×10⁻⁷N magnitude comes from computing near-side minus far-side force.

questions.topic: Rolling bodies — solid vs hollow sphere velocity ratio
questions.question: A solid sphere & a hollow sphere of radius R are rolling down an inclined plane of height h. The ratio of velocities of Solid sphere to Hollow sphere on reaching the bottom is
questions.why: Genuinely new concept (not yet in STUDY_PROGRESS) — energy conservation for a rolling body gives v=sqrt(2gh/(1+k²/R²)), where k²/R² is the body's own moment-of-inertia factor (solid sphere = 2/5, hollow sphere = 2/3). A solid sphere has LESS rotational inertia to spin up, so more energy goes into linear speed — it always rolls faster than a hollow sphere of the same radius down the same incline. Ratio: v_solid/v_hollow = sqrt((1+2/3)/(1+2/5)) = sqrt((5/3)/(7/5)) = sqrt(25/21). Reusable rule: lower k²/R² → faster roller (solid disc/sphere beats hollow cylinder/shell every time).

questions.question: A corona around the moon is seen when we view it on a fogy or misty night. This is due to:
options: Diffraction patterns of air born water droplets
Dispersion of light by air born water droplets
Scattering of light by air born water droplets
Formation of diffused image of moon
questions.why: The coloured rings (corona) around the moon on a misty night come from diffraction of moonlight by tiny suspended water droplets — distinct from a rainbow's dispersion or the blue-sky's scattering.

questions.question: In cold season when lakes freeze, only the top water freezes. Below this layer the water does not freeze and the aquatic life survives. This happens because of:
options: The density of water is maximum at 4°C
Heat convection does not take place in water
Low latent heat of fusion of water
questions.why: Water is anomalous — its density peaks at 4°C, not at 0°C. As a lake cools, the densest (4°C) water sinks to the bottom first; only the coldest, least-dense water stays at the surface and freezes, leaving the bottom liquid at ~4°C where fish survive.

questions.question: The Plank's distribution function is given by:
questions.why: Note the paper's own notation quirk: τ here denotes kT, and this particular option ordering places the Bose-Einstein-style "+1" in the denominator, not the usual "-1" (Planck's standard form uses -1 for bosons/photons). Trust the paper's marked option per its own stated convention; the underlying physics being tested is that photon (boson) statistics use an exponential distribution distinct from the Fermi-Dirac "+1" fermion form. Not independently re-derivable from the text alone without seeing whether this is genuinely a typo in the transcribed options — treat with light caution.

questions.question: At very low temperatures, the heat capacity CV of a solid is:
questions.why: Standard result to recognise, not derive: the Debye T³ law states heat capacity falls as T³ at low temperature (not diverges as (θ/T)³), with prefactor 12π⁴/5. The T-cubed-not-inverted form is the physically sensible piece — heat capacity must go to zero as T→0, ruling out any option with (θ/T)³.

questions.question: The London penetration depth is given by:
questions.why: Standard formula to recognise for superconductivity questions (how far a magnetic field penetrates before being expelled by the Meissner effect) — λ = sqrt(mc²/4πnq²). Memorisation-level fact for this graduate-level topic.

questions.question: The Clausius and Mossotti equation is given by:
questions.why: Standard formula relating a dielectric's permittivity ε to its molecular polarisability α: (ε-1)/(ε+2) = n0α/3ε0. Recognition-level fact.

questions.question: The work done in deforming a body is given by
questions.why: Like the area under a spring's force-extension graph (½kx²), the work stored per unit volume in elastic deformation is the area under the stress-strain line: ½×stress×strain, not the full rectangle.

questions.question: A liquid drop acquires spherical shape due to:
questions.why: Surface tension makes a liquid surface act like a stretched membrane trying to minimise its area — a sphere has the least surface area for a given volume, so free liquid drops naturally pull into spheres.

questions.question: In an orbital motion, the angular momentum vector is:
questions.why: Angular momentum L = r×p is a cross product, so by definition it points perpendicular to the plane containing both r and p — i.e. perpendicular to the orbital plane itself, not lying within it.

questions.question: The Clausius-Clapyron's equation of latent heat is given by:
questions.why: Standard thermodynamics formula relating a phase boundary's slope on a P-T diagram to latent heat L and the volume change (V2-V1) on transition: dP/dT = L/(T·ΔV). Recognition-level fact.

questions.question: The working principle of pressure gauges for measuring static pressure of a fluid flowing in a pipe is based on
questions.why: Bernoulli's theorem (energy conservation along a streamline: pressure + kinetic + potential energy per unit volume is constant) underlies how flow-pressure gauges relate fluid speed to measurable pressure differences.

questions.topic: Thin-film interference — fringe shift with inserted film
questions.question: A double slit experiment is performed with light of wavelength 500 nm. A thin film of thickness 2 μm and refractive index 1.5, is introduced in the path of the upper beam. The location of the central maximum will:
options: Shift downwards by nearly two fringes
Shift upwards by nearly two fringes
questions.why: Inserting a film of thickness t and refractive index μ in one beam's path adds extra optical path (μ-1)t to that beam. Extra fringe shift = (μ-1)t/λ = (0.5×2000nm)/500nm = 2 fringes. Since the film is in the UPPER beam (which now takes longer), the whole pattern shifts toward that beam's side to compensate — upward, by about 2 fringes.

questions.question: In diffraction from a single slit, the angular width of the central maximum does not depend upon:
options: Distance between the slit and the screen
The ratio of wavelength and the slit width
questions.why: Angular width (an angle, θ≈λ/a) depends only on wavelength λ and slit width a — it is purely angular, so the actual screen distance doesn't enter the ANGULAR width formula (though it would affect the physical/linear width on the screen).

questions.question: The minimum value of function x^x exists when x =
questions.why: Let y=x^x, so ln y = x·ln x. Differentiate: (1/y)y' = ln x + 1. Setting y'=0 gives ln x = -1, so x = e^-1 (≈0.368). Standard "log both sides then differentiate" trick for exponent-of-a-variable functions.

questions.topic: Second-order linear ODE (particular integral for e^3x)
questions.question: The solution of the differential equation d²y/dx² − 3dy/dx + 2y = e^3x is
questions.why: Auxiliary equation m²-3m+2=0 factors to (m-1)(m-2)=0, giving roots 1,2, so the complementary function is ae^x+be^2x. For the particular integral with RHS e^3x, try y=Ce^3x: plugging in gives 9C-9C+2C=1 → C=½. Combined: y=ae^x+be^2x+½e^3x.

questions.question: Solution of p√x + q√y = √z is
questions.why: This is Lagrange's linear PDE, solved via the auxiliary equations dx/√x = dy/√y = dz/√z. Integrating dx/√x=dy/√y gives 2√x-2√y=const, i.e. √x-√y=const; combined with the other pair the general solution takes the form √x-√y=f(√x-√z). Recognition-level (Lagrange auxiliary-equation method) for a genuinely new PDE sub-type.

questions.question: The series 2/1² − 3/2² + 4/3² − 5/4² + ⋯ is
questions.why: Term-by-term this is (n+1)/n² with alternating sign. Taking absolute values gives Σ(n+1)/n² ~ Σ1/n, which diverges (harmonic-like), so it's NOT absolutely convergent. But by the alternating series (Leibniz) test, the terms shrink to 0 monotonically, so the alternating series itself DOES converge — that combination (converges, but not absolutely) is the definition of conditionally convergent.

questions.question: Let fn(x) = x^n for all x∈[0,1] and for all positive integers n, then
options: <fn> does not converge at any point
<fn> converges at every point but does not converge uniformly
